title:
TCD News on Instagram: "JUST IN: The Dearborn City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to approve a six-month moratorium on data centers, temporarily pausing new developments while the city creates specific regulations for the facilities.

The final vote comes after the council began considering the moratorium earlier this month. City officials said the six-month pause will give Dearborn time to research and develop zoning rules addressing potential environmental, infrastructure and community impacts from large-scale data centers. 

Dearborn previously removed “Data Processing” as a permitted use from several zoning districts, but officials identified a remaining issue that could allow such operations in the city’s General Industrial district without data-center-specific development standards.

The newly approved moratorium is intended to prevent new data-center projects from moving forward under those existing rules while the city develops permanent regulations.

The vote took place during the Dearborn City Council’s Sept. 22 meeting."

title:
Lima Township adopted Resolution 2026-12 on June 12, 2026 imposing a 12‑month moratorium on establishing, permitting, or constructing any power generating facilities in the township. The board explicitly states it needs time to study and review whether power generating facilities require additional local regulation and to assess potential impacts on land use, environment, public health, safety, and welfare.
The township plans to consider and enact new regulatory and/or zoning ordinances setting standards and potentially designated areas for such facilities, consistent with state and federal law and relevant court precedents. No consultant or vendor has been identified, but the work clearly anticipates legal, planning, and technical analysis to craft an “appropriate regulatory approach” within the moratorium period. This creates a pre‑RFP opening for firms providing land use planning, zoning code updates, environmental impact analysis, and energy/power siting advisory services to help the township design defensible regulations and supporting studies. | Civic IQ
